Document ID: 107858_0203_05_en
Issue 05
Programmers model
snoop_tracker_depth in por_ccg_ra_unit_info, which is the same as parameter RA_NUM_SNPREQS.
To program the number of snoop credits, see:
•
por_ccg_ra_ccprtcl_link0_ctl
•
por_ccg_ra_ccprtcl_link1_ctl
•
por_ccg_ra_ccprtcl_link2_ctl
2.
Program the number request credits using lnk<X>_num_reqcrds_ﬁxed_count for each link in
por_ccg_ha_cxprtcl_link<X>_ctl registers. The total for the 3 links must equal the depth of the
HA request passive buﬀer req_pass_buﬀ_depth in por_ccg_ha_unit_info2, which is the same as
parameter HA_REQ_PASS_BUFF_DEPTH.
3.
Program the number request credits using lnk<X>_num_datcrds_ﬁxed_count for each link in
por_ccg_ha_cxprtcl_link<X>_ctl registers. The total for the 3 links must equal the depth of the
HA request passive buﬀer dat_pass_buﬀ_depth in por_ccg_ha_unit_info2, which is the same as
parameter HA_DAT_PASS_BUFF_DEPTH.
Arm® recommends, programming the CCLA credit manager credit accumulation thresholds in
por_ccla_aux_ctl. Set the crdgnt_crd_count_th for the maximum accumulated credit count before
sending a credit grant message. Set the crdgnt_cycle_count_delay for sending piggyback credits
in the protocol ﬂit headers of existing traﬃc versus sending a dedicated protocol ﬂit with a credit
message.
8.4.9.10 Program CPA functionality in RN SAM
There is a speciﬁc sequence of programming steps that must be followed to set up the RN SAM to
distribute requests to CPAGs.
About this task
This task is part of the requirements to enable communication between local and remote agents.
For the full list of requirements, see Program CML system to enable CML_SMP communication.
To enable CPA, you must program registers in both the RN SAM and HN-F SAM. For the
programming sequence for the HN-F SAM registers, see Program CPA functionality in HN-F LDID-
to-PHYSID LUT.
There are certain rules and restrictions that apply to how CPA can be enabled in a CMN S3(AE)
system. For more information, see SAM support for CML Port Aggregation.
In a two-chip system with CPA enabled, the RN SAM CPA mask of Chip 0 and HN-F SAM CPA
mask of Chip 1 must be programmed to match. Similarly, the RN SAM CPA mask of Chip 1 must
match the HN-F SAM CPA mask of Chip 0.
Procedure
1.
Set the region<n>_pag_en ﬁeld of the cml_port_aggr_mode_ctrl_reg register to 1 and
region<n>_pag_grpid with the relevant group ID for each non-hashed memory region that
belongs to a remote chip and is required to use CPA. This programming enables CPA mode for
the non-hashed memory region and speciﬁes the CPAG that requests must be hashed across.
Copyright © 2023–2025 Arm Limited (or its aﬃliates). All rights reserved.
Non-Conﬁdential
Page 2098 of 2184

@@@PAGE 2099@@@
Arm
® Neoverse™ CMN S3(AE) Coherent Mesh Network
Technical Reference Manual
Document ID: 107858_0203_05_en
Issue 05
Programmers model
2.
Set each bit that must be used to hash requests across CML gateway to 1 in the addr_mask
ﬁeld of the cml_port_aggr_grp<n>_addr_mask register. Set each bit that must be masked from
the hash function to 0. If CPA mode is enabled, RN SAM hashes PA bits[51:6] to distribute
traﬃc between CML gateways. The PA is compared against the addr_mask ﬁeld of the
cml_port_aggr_grp<n>_addr_mask_register. Any PA bit that corresponds to a bit with a 0 value
in the mask register is masked from hashing.
3.
Program the characteristics of the CML gateways for each CPAG by completing the following
steps:
a)
Program the number of CML gateways in each CPAG by setting the num_cxg_pag<n> ﬁeld
in the cml_port_aggr_ctrl_reg register.
b)
Program the CHI node ID of each CML gateway by setting the pag0_tgtid ﬁeld of the same
register.If two CML gateways are being used, then both node IDs must be programmed in
this register. This programming is used by all regions that have CPA enabled.
4.
Repeat the preceding steps for all RN SAMs in the chip.

8.4.9.13 CCLA to CCLA Direct connect mode
CCG enables you to directly connect the CXS interface from the CCLA on one CMN S3(AE) to
the CXS interface of the other. This mode can be used when the lower link layer is not present or
there is a lightweight lower link layer that does not implement the functionality as deﬁned in the
Application Note AES0024. CCG can be built to support a SMP direct connection interface with a
CXS width of 512, by default, or 256 bits. A 256 bit CXS width is only supported when CCLA to
CCLA direct connect mode is used.
Application Note AES0024 is only available upon request.
About this task
The following steps must be followed to enable this Direct connect mode.
1.
Set ull_to_ull_en bit on both sides in CCLA por_ccla_ull_ctl register. Also ull_ﬂit_format is set
with the write that sets ull_to_ull_en. CML_SMP only supports 64B ﬂit format in direct connect
mode. Chip-to-Chip (C2C) also supports the 256B ﬂit format by sending LinkStatus by setting
por_ccla_ull_ctl.send_c2c_link_sts.
2.
After ull_to_ull_en is set on both sides (step 1), set the send_vd_init bit on both sides in CCLA
por_ccla_ull_ctl register.

Program htg_region<X>_hier_enable_address_striping based on the number of clusters

•
Program hashed_target_grp_hnf_target_type_override_cfg_reg<X> to override the HN-F
target type with the CCG. RNI/D uses this information to enable tunneling vs streaming to
remote chip.
3.
HN-F and MXP programming:

8.4.11 Program CMN S3(AE) CML system at runtime
Use this procedure to program a CMN S3(AE) CML system at runtime.
Procedure
1.
Bring up a protocol link. For more information, see Establish protocol link up between CML
gateway and remote CML link.
2.
Add a protocol link in system coherency and DVM domains. For more information, see Entry
and exit protocol links from coherency domains and DVM domains.
3.
Program the remote address range and corresponding RA node ID for each remote memory
region in RN SAM present in CMN S3(AE) RN-F, RN-I, and RN-D. RN SAM must not be
programmed to target RA when enabled for CXSA mode.
If CXSA mode is enabled, programming step 3 is not necessary.
If the software can guarantee that there is no traﬃc to the remote address range
until CML-related initial programming is complete and protocol links are up, then this
programming should be done when programming RN SAMs with local address map.

8.4.12 Establish protocol link up between CML gateway and remote CML
link
Use the following procedure to link up a CML gateway with a remote protocol link that the
gateway can communicate with.
About this task
A protocol link can be established between each CML in CMN S3(AE) and a corresponding remote
CML link that the gateway can communicate with. The term link is used here to refer to a CML
protocol link. Multiple protocol links can be set up simultaneously by extending this sequence for
each link.
Procedure
1.
Poll the lnk<X>_link_en bit in both RA and HA protocol link control (*prtcl_link<X>_ctl) registers
to ensure that the link is enabled.If the link is enabled, then communication on the link can be
established.
2.
Ensure that the link is down and can accept a new link up request by polling the following bits:
a.
Poll the lnk<X>_link_up bits in the RA and HA protocol link control (*prtcl_link<X>_ctl)
registers to ensure that they are clear
b.
Poll the lnk<X>_link_down bits in the RA and HA protocol link status (*prtcl_link<X>_status)
registers to ensure that they are set
c.
Poll the lnk<X>_link_ack bits in the RA and HA protocol link status (*prtcl_link<X>_status)
registers to ensure that they are clear
3.
Set the lnk<X>_link_req bits in the RA and HA protocol link control (*prtcl_link<X>_ctl) registers.
Setting this bit generates a request to link up, which in turn brings up the link.
4.
Poll the following bits in the RA and HA protocol link status (*prtcl_link<X>_status) registers to
ensure that the link up request is accepted:
•
lnk<X>_link_ack
•
lnk<X>_link_down
The hardware acknowledges a link up request by setting the lnk<X>_link_ack bits and then
clearing lnk<X>_link_down bits in RA and HA.
Hardware acknowledgment of link up means that both sides are ready to receive and grant
protocol credits.
5.
Set the lnk<X>_link_up bit in the RA and HA protocol link control (*prtcl_link<X>_ctl) registers
to instruct both sides to start granting credits.
8.4.13 Link down protocol link between CML gateway and remote CML link
Use this procedure to deactivate a protocol link between a CMN S3(AE) CML gateway and a
remote CML link.
Before you begin
Software must ensure that the following conditions are met before initiating a link down sequence:

•
There are no outstanding transactions that require protocol message transfers across the link
for their completion. This condition includes GIC-D in SMP mode.
•
The protocol agents on both sides of the link are conﬁgured to not initiate new transactions

2.
Take the link out of system coherency and DVM domains. For more information, see Entry

About this task
You must follow a speciﬁc process to bring down a protocol link between each CMN S3(AE) CML
gateway and the corresponding remote CML link that the gateway can communicate with. The
term link is used here to refer to a protocol link. Multiple protocol links can be brought down at the
same time by extending this sequence for each link.
CMN S3(AE) CML gateways contain RA, HA, and LA nodes.
Procedure
1.
Ensure that the link is up and can accept a new link down request by polling the following bits
in the RA and HA protocol link control (*prtcl_link<X>_ctl) registers. These bits must be set
before the link can accept a new link down request.:
•
lnk<X>_link_up
•
lnk<X>_link_req
2.
Clear the lnk<X>_link_req bits in the RA and HA protocol link control (*prtcl_link<X>_ctl)
registers to make a link down request.
3.
Poll the lnk<X>_link_ack bit in the RA and HA protocol link status (*prtcl_link<X>_status)
registers to ensure that it is cleared. The hardware acknowledges a link down request by
clearing the lnk<X>_link_ack. After a link down request is accepted, each side must stop
granting local protocol credits and start returning remote protocol credits.
4.
Poll the lnk<X>_link_down bits in the RA and HA protocol link status (*prtcl_link<X>_status)
registers to ensure that each side has received all its protocol credits and is ready to go
down.The hardware sets the lnk<X>_link_down bits to convey that it is ready for the link to go
down.
5.
Clear the lnk<X>_link_up bits in the RA and HA protocol link control (*prtcl_link<X>_ctl)
registers to instruct both sides to deactivate the link.

8.4.14 Entry and exit protocol links from coherency domains and DVM
domains
CMN S3(AE) CML gateway blocks, which contain RA, HA, and LA nodes, can establish a protocol
link with a remote CML link. Each gateway block has software-programmable bits to allow the
protocol links to enter and exit the system coherency domains and DVM domains.
The HA has 2 bits which facilitate snoop coherency domain entry and exit requests and
acknowledgment:
•
The lnk<X>_snoopdomain_req bit of the HA protocol link control (*prtcl_link<X>_ctl) register in
each HA, HA controls snoop coherency domain requests for the link.
•
The lnk<X>_snoopdomain_ack bit of the HA’s protocol link status (*prtcl_link<X>_status)
register, provides acknowledgment and status of the snoop coherency domain requests for the
link.
The RA has 2 bits which facilitate DVM domain entry and exit requests and acknowledgment:
•
The lnk<X>_dvmdomain_req bit in the RA’s protocol link control (*prtcl_link<X>_ctl) register in
each RA, controls DVM domain requests for the link.
•
The lnk<X>_dvmdomain_ack bit in the RA’s protocol link status (*prtcl_link<X>_status) register,
provides acknowledgment and status of the DVM domain requests for the link.
For more information, see RN entry to and exit from Snoop and DVM domains.
8.4.15 Program CML system to enable CHI C2C communication
Use this procedure to enable CML CHI Chip-to-Chip (C2C) communication between diﬀerent
multichip entities.
Before you begin
The CCG must be conﬁgured for CHI C2C and will only support C2C Link 0 in this conﬁguration.
Procedure
1.
Program advertised property registers based on the available supported properties as described
in the CHI C2C speciﬁcation. This includes the CHI C2C credit registers based on the
implemented design. C2C TX packing arbitration can be adjusted by programming the weighted
arbiter message grant registers. Setting 0b01 update_on_grant ﬁeld will update LRU order
on each arbiter grant which will occur on every access/cycle where a new message/data is
packed. Selecting 0b10 will update LRU order only when the maximum number of messages
for a message class, set by the corresponding lru_update_count ﬁeld, have been packed. In all
cases, weights are applied to arbitration before packing and messages for a particular message
class are only packed when the corresponding weight is non-zero. Weights are reduced on each
grant by the number of messages packed for that message class and are reloaded when either
all messages classes have exhausted their weights or when the ones with remaining weights
have their corresponding allow_force_reload ﬁeld set.
2.
Program por_ccla_cfg_ctl.la_c2c_mode_en = 1
Copyright © 2023–2025 Arm Limited (or its aﬃliates). All rights reserved.
Non-Conﬁdential

3.
Follow the link initialization ﬂow sequence in CHI C2C Issue A speciﬁcation Figure B9.1.
4.
Follow the CXS Protocol layer wakeup sequence by programming the LLL to assert a
CXSACTIVEREQ and wait for the CCG ACK.
5.
Program the LLL PHY/controller registers to send the ﬂit format X or Y based on the

8.4.17 Programming optimization for DVMs and CPU events
Certain types of traﬃc like DVMs and CPU events can be optimized on CMN S3(AE) mesh or CML
link based on usage and conﬁguration of a CML gateway block.
This is for CML_SMP only.
For (BTO,BTI)=(1,1) the SnpAttr ﬁeld of non-sync DVMOp requests will be used determine if a
particular request should be sent to a Outer Sharable domain.
Further, incoming DVMSync requests will only be shared to an Outer Sharable domain if a previous
non-sync, Outer Sharable DVMOp request have been handled by the DN. Subsequent DVMSync
requests will not be broadcast to Outer Sharable domains until the next non-sync, Outer Sharable
DVMOp request is received and dispatched by the DN.
The Disable Broadcast on VMF Miss optimization will prevent the broadcast of a VMID-ﬁlterable
non-sync DVMOp from being sent to the Outer Sharable domain.
The aux_ctl.disable_remote_broadcast_on_vmf_miss may only
be enabled if aux_ctl.disable_vmf = 0.To disable DVMOp and
DVMSync optimization the following register programming must be set:
cfg_ctl.broadcast_dvmop_inner = 1cfg_ctl.broadcast_dvmop_outer =
1cfg_ctl.disable_remote_broadcast_on_vmf_miss = 0

conﬁgured for non-SMP connection or is an additional port in a port aggregation group (CPAG):
•
Clear bit corresponding to the LogicalID of that CML gateway block in DN’s
por_dn_domain_cxra register
Additional port of a port aggregation group can be conﬁgured to not send CPU events across a
CML link:

generated for DTM debug watchpoint trigger.

Write 1 to the atbtrigger_en ﬁeld of the por_dt_dtc_ctl register if ATB trigger must be
generated for DTM debug watchpoint trigger.
3.
Write 1 to the cc_enable ﬁeld of the por_dt_trace_control register to enable cycle count.
4.
Write 0 to the dt_wait_for_trigger ﬁeld of the por_dt_dtc_ctl register if no cross trigger is
required.
5.
Write 1 to the dt_en ﬁeld of the por_dt_dtc_ctl register.

8.4.19.1 Set up PMU counters
Use this procedure to set up the PMU counters correctly.
Procedure
1.
Ensure that the NIDEN input is asserted for any trace and PMU operations.
2.
Program (dev)_pmu_event_sel register in the devices or XP.
3.
Program the pmevcnt{0..3}_input_sel ﬁelds of the por_dtm_pmu_conﬁg register to select PMU
event counter inputs. The input can be from one of the following:
•
A watchpoint.
•
Selected events from the devices or XP, depending on step 2.
4.
Program the following por_dtm_pmu_conﬁg register ﬁelds to select the paired top global PMU
counters:
•
pmevcnt_paired
•
pmevcnt{0..3}_global_num
5.
Program the pmevcnt{01, 23}_combined ﬁelds of the por_dtm_pmu_conﬁg for any combined
local PMU counters.
6.
Write 1 to the pmu_en ﬁeld of the dtm_pmu_conﬁg register.
7.
Program the cntcfg ﬁeld of the por_dt_pmcr register to pair the 32-bit global counters to make
a 64-bit counter.
8.
Write 1 to the ovﬂ_intr_en ﬁeld of the por_dt_pmcr register to enable interrupts on
INTREQPMU on any global counter overﬂow.
9.
Write 1 to the pmu_en ﬁeld of the por_dt_pmcr register to start PMU operation.
10. Write 1 to the dt_en ﬁeld of the por_dt_dtc_ctl register
8.4.19.2 Program PMU snapshot
Use this procedure to set up the PMU snapshot functionality.
Before you begin
The NIDEN input must be asserted for any trace and PMU operation.
About this task
For a system with multiple DTCs, the sub-DTC maintains snapshot status for the DTM within its
own domain.
Procedure
1.
Program PMU counters as described in Set up PMU counters.
2.
Write 1 to the ss_req ﬁeld of the por_dt_pmsrr register. This action causes the DTC to send a
PMU snapshot instruction. On receiving this instruction, the DTM sends PMU snapshot packets
to the DTC.

8.4.19.3 Program PMU counter overﬂow interrupt
Use this procedure to set up the PMU counter overﬂow interrupt.
Before you begin
The NIDEN input must be asserted for any trace and PMU operation.
Procedure
1.
Program PMU counters as described in Set up PMU counters.
2.
Write 1 to the ovﬂ_intr_en ﬁeld of the por_dt_pmcr register. Overﬂow of any PMU counter
causes INTREQPMU to assert.
3.
Write 1 to the ovﬂ_intr_en ﬁeld in the all other por_dt_pmcr registers if your system has
multiple DTCs.
4.
Poll the pmovsr[7:0] ﬁeld of the por_dt_pmovsr register when INTREQPMU is asserted to see
which global counter causes the interrupt. For multiple DTCs, all por_dt_pmovsr registers must
be polled.
5.
Write 1 to the corresponding bit in the pmovsr_clr[7:0] ﬁeld of the por_dt_pmovsr_clr register
to clear INTREQPMU.

Pseudo-migration of cached data
For a given cacheline address, CHI protocol requires an interconnect (ICN) to not send Snoops
until CompAck or Data are received at HN-F. However, there are exceptions to this requirement in
systems with CML enabled in the following circumstance.
•
If the request types are:
◦
ReadOnce* or ReadNoSnp
◦
WriteNoSnp* or WriteUnique*
◦
Atomics
The reason for this behavior is because of protocol diﬀerences between CHI and CML_SMP with
respect to presence of CompAck on these requests. This violation is acceptable because the initial
and ﬁnal cache state on these requests is “Invalid” .
Copyright © 2023–2025 Arm Limited (or its aﬃliates). All rights reserved.
Non-Conﬁdential
Page 2123 of 2184

@@@PAGE 2124@@@
Arm
® Neoverse™ CMN S3(AE) Coherent Mesh Network
Technical Reference Manual
Document ID: 107858_0203_05_en
Issue 05
Protocol feature compliance
•
If the CML gateway block receives a WriteClean. This exception happens because the CML
gateway block synthesizes the Snoop here on a CHI WriteClean, and it assumes that the RN-
F must already see completion for prior request before RN-F dispatches WriteClean. This
exception is acceptable because RN-F has already issued WriteClean for the same cacheline. It
cannot do that unless the prior request to the same cacheline has received completion.
A.5 CXL support
The following provides the CXL information used for CML support.
CMN S3(AE) supports CXL.mem (Type 3) and CXL.cache (Type 1) functionality for host
implementation and is compliant with Compute Express Link (CXL) speciﬁcation revision 2.0 dated
October 2020 and CXL 3 revision 3.0 version 1.0 release candidate dated June 2022 with the
following limitations:
•
QoS telemetry: Incoming CXL DevLoad is mapped to CHI Cbusy. For more information, see
Completer Busy indication.
•
CXL registers implemented in CCG can be accessed through the corresponding CCG’s APB
port. List of registers implemented in CCG and their corresponding oﬀsets can be found in
CXLAPB register summary. Same registers are implemented in CCLA register space and these
can be accessed using CMN conﬁguration read or write accesses. By default access to these
CXL registers is provided through CMN conﬁguration mechanism and software must set
enable_cxl_regs_apb_access bit in por_ccla_aux_ctl register to allow access through the APB
port. All the other registers as deﬁned by CXL speciﬁcation are expected to be implemented in
CXL controller IP or SoC.
•
In host mode, system software is expected to map the contents from HDM decoder to CMN
S3(AE) HN SAM and RN SAM structures.
◦
This programming is required to route CXL.mem traﬃc to appropriate CXL 2.0 or CXL 3.0
memory device. Host HDM decoder structures, one per CHBCR space as deﬁned by CXL
speciﬁcation, are expected to be implemented outside CMN S3(AE).
◦
CMN S3(AE) supports all memory interleaving options as deﬁned by CXL 2.0 speciﬁcation
including 3, 6, and 12 way interleaving as deﬁned by CXL 2.0 ECN.
•
Inbound viral from a CXL device is terminated at the corresponding gateway block and can be
optionally reported as CMN S3(AE) uncorrectable error (UE).
•
MemSpecRead is supported
•
DevLoad is supported
•
APB port is provided for external controller IP to access CXL registers implemented in CCG.
This is a 32 bit port where writes must have PSTRB[3:0] = 0xF.
•
CMN S3(AE) supports a maximum of 16 CCGs for CXL.mem Type 3 device attachment.
•
CMN S3(AE) supports CXL 2.0 IDE and CXL 3.0 for Host implementation. IDE is also
supported for CXL 2.0 and CXL 3.0 Type 3 device
•
Host isolation is supported for CXL 2.0 and CXL3.0
Copyright © 2023–2025 Arm Limited (or its aﬃliates). All rights reserved.
Non-Conﬁdential

@@@PAGE 2125@@@
Arm
® Neoverse™ CMN S3(AE) Coherent Mesh Network
Technical Reference Manual
Document ID: 107858_0203_05_en
Issue 05
Protocol feature compliance
•
CXL Type 1 Multiple Cache-ID is supported. Each Type 1 device supports up to 16 Caching
agents. Programming of the CXL Caching agents is similar to the SMP cache-ids.

A.7 CHI C2C Support
The following provides the CHI C2C information used for CML support.
CMN S3(AE) supports CHI C2C functionality for the host and is compliant with AMBA CHI C2C
issue B Version dated August 29th, 2024, with the following limitations:
•
Max Number of request resource plane supported for transmitter and receiver is two.
•
If the CHI C2C accelerator only supports one request resource plane and supports DVM and
SMMU traﬃc, then the request resource plane needs to be non-blocking
•
If the CHI C2C accelerator does not support request shared credits or data shared credits
◦
WritePush_Support_Tx needs to be set to false
◦
If only one request resource plane is supported, DVMPush_Support_Tx needs to be set to
false.
•
Refer to CHI C2C Property Support for the speciﬁc property support.

Appendix B Signal descriptions
CMN S3(AE) signals are composed of a base name along with identiﬁers that indicate unique
product conﬁgurations.
Because there are multiple identical interfaces in CMN S3(AE), the signal names that this appendix
describes are often only root names. The actual signal name includes a port-speciﬁc identiﬁer
suﬃx.
The system conﬁguration determines which of the signals are used in a particular system.
Unless speciﬁed otherwise, CMN S3(AE) signals are active-HIGH.
B.1 ACE-Lite and AXI Interface signals
All signal names for CMN S3(AE) ACE-Lite and AXI interface consist of a RootName.
CMN S3(AE) interfaces use RootName within a fully speciﬁed signal as follows:
CMN S3(AE) ACE-Lite and AXI interface signalname == RootName_[S|M]<#a>_NID#b, where:
S|M
Deﬁnes either a Completer or Requester interface.
#a
Deﬁnes an optional interface identiﬁer for a node that can support multiple AMBA®
interfaces.
#b
Deﬁnes the node ID corresponding to the speciﬁc interface.
Multi-bit signals append the bit-range identiﬁer included in the RootName to the end of the full
signalname.
Copyright © 2023–2025 Arm Limited (or its aﬃliates). All rights reserved.

WUSER_S[0] acts as a WDATACHK valid signal when the DATACHECK_EN parameter is enabled:
•
If WUSER_S[0] = 0, the RN-I or RN-D synthesizes the correct WDATACHK value before
sending it on CHI write data.
•
If WUSER_S[0] = 1, the RN-I or RN-D uses WDATACHK pin value to drive on CHI write data.
If the DATACHECK_EN parameter is disabled, the WUSER_S[0] input is ignored.
RUSER_S[0] acts as an RDATACHK valid signal. Since the RN-I or RN-D always drives the
RDATACHK value, RUSER_S[0] is set to 1 when DATACHECK_EN parameter is enabled. If the
DATACHECK_EN parameter is disabled, RUSER_S[0] output is set to 0.
B.1.2 AXI and ACE-Lite Requester interface signals
HN-I, SBSX, and MTSX have an AXI or ACE-Lite Requester interface.

RUSER_M[0] acts as an RDATACHK valid signal when DATACHECK_EN parameter is enabled:
•
If RUSER_M[0] = 0, the SBSX or HN-I synthesizes the correct RDATACHK value before sending
it on CHI read data response.
•
If RUSER_M[0] = 1, the SBSX or HN-I uses the RDATACHK pin value to drive CHI read data
response.
If the DATACHECK_EN parameter is disabled, the RUSER_M[0] input is ignored.
WUSER_M[0] acts as a WDATACHK valid signal. Because the SBSX or HN-I always drives the
WDATACHK value, WUSER_M[0] is set to 1 when DATACHECK_EN parameter is enabled. If the
DATACHECK_EN parameter is not enabled, the WUSER_M[0] output is driven to 0.

B.1.4 HN-I and HN-P AxID signal properties and encodings
The size and encodings of the AxID signals on the AXI or ACE-Lite interface are diﬀerent for HN-I
and HN-P.
The term peer-to-peer refers to requests from an RN-I or RN-D that is connected to a PCIe-
RC to an HN-I that is connected to a PCIe-RC or an HN-P. The pcie_mstr_present bit in the
por_rn{i,d}_cfg_ctl register indicates whether an RN-I or RN-D is connected to a PCIe-RC. Also,
dis_awid_to_hni_hnp_cxra bit in the por_rn{i,d}_cfg_ctl register, must remain set to 0 to enable
passing the AxID signal to HN-I and HN-P.
The physical_mem_en attribute can be enabled in the HN-I SAM for an address range where
Normal memory ordering is required. For example, prefetchable MMIO or non-prefetchable MMIO
space which is mapped as Normal memory.
The following table shows the AxID properties and encodings for the HN-I and HN-P.
Table B-8: HN-I AxID signal encodings
AxID width
Downstream memory
type
Request source
Encoding
Any
AxID[3:0] = HN-I SAM order region
encoding

B.2 APB interface signals
HN-D nodes have an APB interface to support the connection of an external APB Requester
device.
Each CML Gateway (CCG) block has an APB port for CXL controller IP to access CXL deﬁned
registers implemented in them.
All signal names in this section are only a root name indicated as RootName.
CMN S3(AE) interfaces use RootName within a more fully speciﬁed signal name
as follows: CMN S3(AE) interface signal name == RootName_NID#, where #
represents the node ID corresponding to the speciﬁc interface.

DFTSCANMODE
Input
During functional mode, the HN-F SLC and SF RAM set address and write data inputs
satisfy RAM hold timing constraints using pipeline behavior. The set address and write
data are only clocked and enabled the cycle before the RAMs are accessed, and are held
the cycle that the RAM clock asserts. The RAM hold constraints are not guaranteed
during ATPG test, because random data is shifted into the ﬂops that control the set
address and write data ﬂop enables. This allows the set address and write data to change
in the same cycle as a RAM access, violating the RAM hold constraints.
This signal addresses the hold constraints during ATPG test. It is used to force the RAM
set address and write data ﬂop enables LOW in the cycle that RAM clocks are enabled
during ATPG test.
The combination of the functional pipeline behavior and this override logic enable holds
MCPs to be used on the RAM set address and write data inputs in the implementation
ﬂow and during static timing analysis.
Tie LOW if
unused

B.4 CHI interface signals
CMN S3(AE) uses channels that form an inbound and outbound CHI interface for each device
using signals that form each channel in a speciﬁc interface.
The AMBA® CHI Architecture Speciﬁcation deﬁnes four channels:
•
Request (REQ)
•
Response (RSP)
•
Snoop (SNP)
•
Data (DAT)
All signal names in this section are only a root name, RootName. CMN S3(AE)
interfaces use RootName within a more fully speciﬁed signal name as follows:
•
CMN S3(AE) interface signal name == RootName_NID#, where # is the node ID
corresponding to the speciﬁc interface.
B.4.1 Per-channel interface signals
For communication between devices, each channel includes a Transmit (TX) and a Receive (RX)
port, with various interface signals traveling from TX to RX.
Connection of CHI interfaces between two devices requires cross-coupling of the
TX* and RX* signals between the two devices, as required by the CHI architecture.

CMN S3(AE) interface signal name == RootName_NID#, where # represents the
node ID corresponding to the speciﬁc interface.

Issue 05
Signal descriptions
If a CPU or IO requester implements its EVENT_OUT indication as a single signal, multicycle pulse,
event handling and stitching logic external to CMN S3(AE) must convert this EVENT_OUT to a two-
signal, four-phase handshake for connection to CMN S3(AE)’s EVENTOREQ and EVENTOACK interface.
Likewise if a CPU or IO requester implements its EVENT_IN port as a single signal, receiving a
multicycle pulse, event handling and stitching logic external to CMN S3(AE) must convert CMN
S3(AE)’s two-signal, four-phase handshake EVENTIREQ output to a pulse and synthesize a EVENTIACK
response. Any such stitching logic must account for any asynchronous domain crossings.

Conventions
The following subsections describe conventions used in Arm documents.
Glossary
The Arm Glossary is a list of terms used in Arm documentation, together with deﬁnitions for
those terms. The Arm Glossary does not contain terms that are industry standard unless the Arm
meaning diﬀers from the generally accepted meaning.
See the Arm Glossary for more information: developer.arm.com/glossary.
Typographic conventions
Arm documentation uses typographical conventions to convey speciﬁc meaning.
Convention
Use
italic
Citations.
bold
Terms in descriptive lists, where appropriate.
monospace
Text that you can enter at the keyboard, such as commands, ﬁle and program names, and
source code.
monospace underline
A permitted abbreviation for a command or option. You can enter the underlined text
instead of the full command or option name.
<and>
Encloses replaceable terms for assembler syntax where they appear in code or code
fragments.
For example:
MRC p15, 0, <Rd>, <CRn>, <CRm>, <Opcode_2>
SMALL CAPITALS
Terms that have speciﬁc technical meanings as deﬁned in the Arm® Glossary. For example,
IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED, IMPLEMENTATION SPECIFIC, UNKNOWN, and UNPREDICTABLE.

system will not work.

Signal level
The level of an asserted signal depends on whether the signal is active-HIGH or active-LOW.
Asserted means:
•
HIGH for active-HIGH signals.
•
LOW for active-LOW signals.
Lowercase n
At the start or end of a signal name, n denotes an active-LOW signal.
